name: Why Restarts Are Dangerous
title: Why Restarts Are Dangerous
description: Restarts concentrate risk: systems in unknown states, operators under pressure, and the original fault possibly still present. Most restart accidents come from rushing.
how_it_works: Treat every restart as a planned operation: verify state, confirm the fault is cleared, and follow the sequence. Rushing restarts creates the second emergency.
key_points: Unknown states plus pressure equals risk.
Verify state and fault clearance first.
requirements: Defined shutdown/fault state; restart prerequisites and sequence; verification before resuming normal operation.
standards: Startup/shutdown procedure practice; safety instrumented system reset requirements.
citations: Industry startup/shutdown procedure guidance.
IEC 61511 requirements on SIF reset and restart.

name: Cascading Failure Recovery
title: Cascading Failure Recovery
description: Cascades need careful sequencing: restore in an order that doesn't re-trigger the cascade. Understanding the cascade's mechanism guides the recovery order.
how_it_works: Analyze the cascade mechanism, define a restoration order that avoids re-triggering, and restore in islands that are verified before interconnection. Patience prevents re-collapse.
requirements: Defined shutdown/fault state; restart prerequisites and sequence; verification before resuming normal operation.
standards: Startup/shutdown procedure practice; safety instrumented system reset requirements.
citations: Industry startup/shutdown procedure guidance.
IEC 61511 requirements on SIF reset and restart.

name: Recovery Automation
title: Recovery Automation
description: Automation speeds recovery: orchestrated restarts, automated verification, self-healing. But automation needs its own verification - automated wrong is fast wrong.
how_it_works: Automate well-understood recovery steps, keep human checkpoints for judgment calls, and test automation in drills. Monitor automated recovery - it can fail too.
requirements: Defined shutdown/fault state; restart prerequisites and sequence; verification before resuming normal operation.
